subject: Post-demo: Encryption & BYOK operational questions + contract clauses
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finbank.com>, Compliance Team <compliance@finbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Encryption & BYOK operational questions + contract clauses

Hi Sanjay / FinBank compliance team —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and the operational/contract asks we discussed so we can get you a formal response by early next week. I put technical/ops asks first, then contract/legal bullets.

What we covered (summary)
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 with mutual TLS support for customer-facing endpoints; optional client certs for private deployments.
- At-rest: AES-256 encryption for model artifacts and persisted embeddings; metadata and logs encrypted at rest.
- BYOK: We support three BYOK patterns: (1) Cloud KMS envelope keys (AWS KMS / Google KMS / Azure Key Vault), (2) Bring-Your-Own-HSM via KMIP or hybrid key wrap before import, (3) External key-wrapping service (customer-managed wrap/unwrap).
- Audit/logging: Token-level and request-level audit logs with optional redaction sampling; retention configurable per customer.

Operational asks (we need your input)
1) Residency: You asked about keeping logs and PII in us-east-1 — is that a firm requirement or preferred? Please confirm if all telemetry + persisted content must remain in us-east-1.
2) KMS choice: Which BYOK pattern do you prefer for an initial pilot? Options: AWS KMS CMKs (us-east-1), customer HSM (on-prem or partner HSM), or external key-wrapping SaaS.
3) Key ops: Confirm rotation policy window (recommended: rotate envelope keys every 90 days; CMKs left per KMS provider defaults). Any regulatory cadence we must follow?
4) Logging retention: You mentioned 13 months for audit logs — confirm retention period and whether logs must be immutable/append-only with WORM.
5) Evidence: Attached is a first-pass SOC2 evidence request workbook. Please flag any additional artifacts you require (e.g., KMS key usage logs, HSM attestation, KDF parameters).

Contract/legal asks we discussed
- Data segregation clause: explicit language that FinBank data (inputs + embeddings) is logically segregated and not used to train models.
- BYOK warranty: need language that prevents Redwood from having access to unwrapped customer keys; we can provide an attestation for envelope-handling.
- Incident SLA: proposed notification window for suspected key compromise is 1 hour for confirmed incidents and 24 hours for suspected.

Next steps and owners
- You (FinBank): confirm residency requirement + preferred BYOK pattern by EOD Friday (Sanjay).
- Redwood (Grace / Aditya): we will prepare a short playbook for the selected BYOK pattern that includes steps to provision, rotate, and deprovision keys; target delivery: Tue 2028-06-18.
- Redwood legal (Marissa): draft suggested contract language for BYOK and incident notification; target: Tue 2028-06-18.

Attachments: redwood-byo-kms-playbook.pdf (overview), soc2-evidence-request.xlsx (spreadsheet of artifacts)

If anything above is off from the call notes, please flag. I can set up a focused 30-min session with our crypto engineer if you want a deeper dive.

Thanks,

Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Jun 2028 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Encryption & BYOK operational questions + contract clauses

Great notes, Grace — a few technical clarifications to add before we finalize the playbook: 

1) Network in-transit: our hosted API supports TLS 1.3; for Dedicated/Private we can enable mTLS between customer network and inference nodes. For Private VPC we can also terminate TLS at the customer load balancer if required.

2) BYOK patterns (tradeoffs)
- Cloud KMS (recommended initial route): easiest integration, preserves CMK ownership semantics, audit logs via CloudTrail / equivalent. Envelope keys handled by Redwood runtime; Redwood never stores unwrapped CMKs.
- HSM / KMIP: supports FIPS 140-2/3 requirements and on-prem custody—more operational uplift and lead time (~4–8 weeks provisioning depending on vendor).
- External wrap/unwrap: provides strongest control when customers refuse cloud KMS import; requires low-latency connectivity to wrap endpoint for token issuance.

3) Key rotation: we recommend rotating envelope keys every 90 days; CMK rotation can follow provider defaults (annual), but we can align to customer policy if they require more frequent rotation.

4) Audit logs: we can provide an access-friendly bundle: (a) token-level access logs, (b) KMS key usage records (when using cloud KMS), (c) HSM attestation reports. For hosted customers we retain query logs 90 days by default; retention extension to 13 months available as an enterprise option.

I'll incorporate the above into the playbook. Grace — can you confirm FinBank asked for WORM retention, or just immutability assertions? Sanjay: quick confirm on that and whether 13 months is acceptable.

-Aditya

Aditya Rao
Principal Product Manager, Security
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finbank.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinBank Security <security@finbank.com>, Compliance Team <compliance@finbank.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jun 2028 08:07:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Encryption & BYOK operational questions + contract clauses

Thanks Grace and Aditya — good summary. A few clarifications from FinBank side:

- Residency: This is a firm requirement for the pilot. All customer data (including logs containing PII or request metadata) must remain in us-east-1. Any replication outside us-east-1 must be disabled.
- BYOK: We prefer to start with AWS KMS CMKs in us-east-1 for speed, with a plan to evaluate HSM (Thales/Volt) for production later. Please assume initial pilot will use Envelope keys with CMKs in our AWS account.
- Key ops: FinBank rotation policy is 90 days for envelope keys; CMKs rotated per provider (we will provide rotation cadence later).
- Logging retention: 13 months retention required; logs must be append-only with tamper-evidence. We do not need WORM hardware but need attestable immutability (sha256 chains, signed bundles acceptable).
- Evidence: we'll fill the SOC2 workbook and attach our KMS attestation template.

Action items from FinBank
- I'll send the filled SOC2 sheet and KMS attestation template by EOD Friday (Sanjay).

Action items for Redwood
- Provide BYOK playbook (steps to configure CMK in customer account + envelope integration) and a short FAQ on expected latencies when calling the wrap/unwrap flow.
- Provide sample contract language for key access, incident notification windows, and data residency guarantees.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Security, FinBank
sanjay.rao@finbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@finbank.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Encryption & BYOK operational questions + contract clauses

Thanks — noted. I'll draft suggested contractual language covering:

- Data residency commitments (us-east-1 only, no cross-region backups unless explicitly enabled and approved)
- BYOK clause that specifies Redwood cannot access unwrapped customer keys and will provide attestation reports for envelope operations
- Incident notification SLA language (1 hour confirmed, 24 hours suspected)
- Audit log retention and immutability (13 months, signed bundles or equivalent tamper-evident mechanism)

I'll share a redline by Tue 2028-06-18, and loop in Legal for final signoff. Grace/Aditya: please send any technical snippets you want included in the exhibit (e.g., sample CloudTrail entries, KMS key policy snippet).

-marissa
